Use a matched BERT4Rec ablation: same initialization, splits, architecture, optimizer, batches, masked targets, and seed 42; change only negative selection. Common random numbers support paired comparisons ([Heikes et al.](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/003754977602700301)). Operationally, isolate RNG streams for training-example selection, masking, dropout, and negative sampling so mining’s extra draws cannot change subsequent examples. Match candidate pools where applicable; exclude known training positives without consulting held-out labels. Predeclare mining pool size, refresh schedule, and loss weighting. Equal updates isolate sampling effects per update; equal GPU time measures practical efficiency and must charge mining, refresh, validation, and diagnostics. Report both where budget permits, retaining 200 batches/epoch and the 200-epoch ceiling.

Predeclare checkpoint eligibility, validation frequency, tie-breaking, and trial allocation. Compare fixed-update checkpoints alongside the common time-budget endpoint; selecting each method’s best of differently sized checkpoint searches adds selection bias. Repeated tuning on the same validation users can overfit the selection criterion ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Record every attempted configuration; treat validation gains as exploratory until independent final evaluation. For uncertainty, retain paired per-user hit indicators on identical candidates. Compute Δmacro = ¼Σcategory mean(hit_mined − hit_uniform); bootstrap user pairs within each category, then recompute the equally weighted macro difference. Report category differences, discordant counts, and a paired interval. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and candidate sets; they exclude seed variability and adaptive-selection bias.

With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR@10 by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR@10 by 0.125 points. Ranking against 99 sampled negatives measures the pinned 100-candidate task; sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model orderings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Keep evaluation seed/candidates fixed and avoid claims of full-catalog or deployment superiority.
